detail.longDescription: Consider the following class Point and its metaclass PointMeta . What happens if I omit the super call in __init__ method of PointMeta class, is there any difference in behavior? class PointMeta(type): def __new__(cls, name, bases, attrs): return super().__new__(cls, name, bases, attrs) def __init__(self, name, bases, attrs): super().__init__(name, bases, attrs) # more logic here class Point(metaclass=PointMeta): def __init__(self, x, y): self.x = x self.y = y p1 = Point(1, 1) I have tried it and seem to see no difference. The newly created class returned by __new__ method of PointMeta already contains all its attributes, is it still necessary to make the super call in __init__ ? I have seen large codebases still make the super call, why? Can someone help with an example where making/not making the super call can make a difference?
